title: Precision path interoperability constraints and KV-cache notes
content:
Status: draft; purpose: capture kernel-level constraints and runtime scheduling interactions for the low-precision execution paths (INT8, FP8, GPTQ, AWQ) and how the KV-cache and batching layer must adapt.

Summary
This doc records concrete constraints and compatibility rules we've discovered while prototyping mixed-precision execution paths. It focuses on the intersection of three components: (1) kernel contracts and layout requirements for different quant formats, (2) the scheduler/batcher behavior that must be aware of precision constraints to maintain latency and throughput SLOs, and (3) KV-cache semantics when keys/values are produced/consumed by quantized kernels or when evict/fill paths cross precision boundaries.

Goals
- Enumerate kernel ABI expectations for INT8/FP8/GPTQ/AWQ kernels that the runtime must enforce.
- Define scheduling rules and fallback routes when matching kernels are unavailable.
- Specify KV-cache invariants and migration/fallback strategies if cached KV blocks are from a different precision than the requested model variant.
- Produce a small test matrix and microbenchmarks to validate trade-offs (accuracy, latency, memory).

Kernel constraints (high level)
1) Weight memory layout and alignment
   - INT8/GPTQ/AWQ kernels assume tightly packed int8 weight tiles in row-major order with 32B alignment for vectorized loads.
   - FP8 kernels expect 16-bit-aligned buffers with an 8-byte header per weight tensor describing scale/zero-point metadata when using per-block quantization.
   - Runtime must expose a canonical layout converter for on-the-fly reformatting if model artifact uses a different convention. Avoid conversion in hot path unless cached formatted weights are available.

2) Per-channel vs per-tensor scales
   - GPTQ/AWQ often use per-channel scales for matmul outputs. Kernels will expose whether they accept per-channel scale arrays or only per-tensor.
   - ABI: kernel descriptor must include scale_ptr (nullable) + scale_stride to support both. Null implies per-tensor only.

3) Accumulator precision and reduction semantics
   - INT8 and AWQ kernels rely on int32 accumulators then requantize; FP8 kernels often use float32 accumulation on CUDA/ROCm with later casting.
   - For identical numerical results across paths, define reduction order and rounding behavior in descriptor (reduce_left_to_right bool; rounding_mode enum).

4) KV cache production/consumption contract
   - KV tensors produced by quantized transformer attention kernels may be in compressed/quantized format. The cache store needs two modes: raw_format (same layout as kernel output) and canonical_fp16/float32 representation.
   - Cache writes: kernel should indicate produced_precision field (one of: int8, awq, gptq, fp8, fp16, float32) plus format_id string.
   - Cache reads: scheduler must prefer raw_format hits when requested precision == produced_precision. If mismatch, runtime must either (a) convert on read (costly), (b) re-compute using unquantized fallback model, or (c) route to compatible kernel that accepts the stored format.

Scheduling & batching implications
1) Precision-aware queueing
   - Each worker/gpu queue maintains sub-queues by precision family. This prevents enqueuing an INT8-only kernel on a GPU instance set up for FP8 fast paths.
   - Policy: for tight latency SLOs, prefer same-precision batching even if batch utilization is slightly lower. For throughput-first contracts, allow cross-precision coalescing only when kernels share identical memory layouts and accumulator types.

2) Dynamic fallback & rollout paths
   - If a cluster lacks INT8/GPTQ optimized kernels for a model version, fallback options in order: (a) INT8->FP16 compatible kernel (if supports dequantized weights), (b) FP8 kernel (if supports mapping), (c) software dequantization then FP16 matmul. Documented fallback chain must be encoded in model manifest.

3) Cost of on-the-fly layout conversion
   - Measured conversion tax: reformatting a 2GB weight shard from GPTQ format to INT8 tiled format is O(N) and may take tens of ms on CPU/host; unacceptable on hot-path. Action: preformat weights during model load; keep a single canonical hot-format in device memory. Eviction policy must prefer keeping hot-format for currently scheduled precision.

KV-cache specific rules and invariants
1) Cache key for format-awareness
   - Cache key = (model_id, model_version, precision_tag, format_id, seq_position_block). precision_tag must be included. This enables safe reuse only when precision matches.

2) Migration strategies
   - Transparent conversion: when storage is canonical FP16 but request wants INT8 kernels, we can quantize cached FP16 KVs into INT8 on read and write a backfilled int8 representation if space allows. Prioritize conversion for recent hot-blocks.
   - Recompute-on-miss: if conversion cost > threshold and model allows partial recompute, prefer computing KVs for new precision instead of converting. Threshold tunable per-customer SLA.

3) Eviction & fragmentation
   - Mixed-precision caches lead to fragmentation. Recommended allocator: segregated pools per precision, with an LRU within each pool and a global swapping policy using age-and-frequency heuristics.

Compatibility matrix (proposal)
- Row = produced_precision; Column = requested_kernel_precision; cells: allowed/convert/recompute.
- Example rows: produced=int8, requested=int8 -> allowed; produced=int8, requested=fp16 -> convert on read (fast dequant); produced=gptq, requested=int8 -> convert only if same tile alignment; else recompute.

Tests and microbenchmarks
- Simple microbench suite: generate KV tensors for standard Llama-2 13B layers under each quant scheme, measure: write latency, read+convert latency, hit-rate impact for prefixes of 16/64/128 tokens, and accuracy delta after conversion.
- Stress test: mixed-precision traffic simulator hitting scheduling logic with configurable ratios (INT8:FP8:FP16 = 70:20:10) to validate queue isolation and throughput.

Open questions / TODOs
- Tile descriptors: finalize compact header format for weight tiles that supports both AWQ and GPTQ metadata without doubling header size. (Owner: Rina)
- Hardware offload: can newer Ampere/Blackwell kernels perform FP8 accumulation with int8-like memory layout? If yes, we can unify some code paths. (Action: Ethan to benchmark)
- Runtime API: extend model manifest schema to include fallback_chain and supported_format_ids. Need PR to schema repo. (ENG-1198)

Next steps
1) Add canonical layout converter to runtime/lib/format_conversion; mark hot-format caches pinned during model load.
2) Implement precision_tag in KV-cache key and change eviction policy to segregated pools.
3) Create microbench harness and run across target hardware (A100, H100, RTX) to populate conversion cost table.
4) Draft runtime spec PR describing kernel descriptor fields (produced_precision, format_id, scale_ptr, accumulator_type, rounding_mode).

Notes to reviewers
- This is intentionally a pragmatic, implementation-first draft. I expect API names to change. Focus feedback on invariants (cache key must include precision) and scheduling policy trade-offs for latency SLOs.

References & links
